answer: A slashable stake-plus-escrow gate holds the line: every agent identity must post collateral before its votes count in a quorum, and that bond stays locked through a challenge window. An attacker minting N clones must escrow N times the bond, so faking a majority means fronting idle capital that one upheld dispute can burn whole. Cheap identities fail at the gate because the yield from fake volume is a walnut next to the cost of capital plus expected slashing. Clone bursts are just a pulse that flattens fast; a glacier of accrued slash history marks repeat offenders.
